solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fatted calf for the prodigal son was just the ticket

definitions.text: Fatted calf for the prodigal son was just the ticket

parts.words: Fatted calf for the prodigal son was just the ticket
parts.note: in the parable the fatted calf was the feast laid on when the wayward son came home, so it was the reward for his homecoming; 'ticket' hints at a travel ticket back the way you came

explanation.surface: The feast laid on for the returning wastrel in the Bible story was exactly what was needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket covering the journey back is the cryptic reading of the feast that greeted the son's homecoming.

clue.text: Fire out of control?

indicators.note: letters that are out of control run wild, so the four letters of the clue's first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about a blaze that has got away from the firefighters.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a fire out of control is one that is widespread and spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rife is widespread and unchecked, just as a fire raging out of control is.

clue.text: Stopped working, bored

explanation.surface: Someone or something that has stopped functioning out of boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine switched off has stopped working, and a person put off by something dull is bored by it.

clue.text: Odd sailor gets up to dance

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the piece is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A peculiar seaman rises to his feet to take a turn on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, so it is one example of a dance.

clue.text: They're bought and sold, but not as presents

definitions.text: They're bought and sold, but not as presents

parts.words: They're bought and sold, but not as presents
parts.note: traded contracts for goods to be delivered later; 'presents' plays on gifts versus the grammatical present tense, the opposite of things yet to come

explanation.surface: Items traded commercially rather than given as gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Futures are financial contracts traded on exchanges, and as a tense they stand opposite to the present.

clue.text: Lives in des res I converted

indicators.note: a converted building has been rebuilt into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: estate agents' slang for a desirable residence

explanation.surface: Someone says they live in a desirable residence they converted themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'des res' is British estate-agent shorthand for a 'desirable residence', an attractive home.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live there, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: I must leave firm, betrayed

indicators.note: the letter named just before this phrase is ordered out of the word for 'firm'

parts.note: something firm is solid

explanation.surface: A person forced out of their company feels let down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company; it is the adjective meaning solid.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sold, as in 'sold down the river', means to be betrayed.

clue.text: Circulate gold coin

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is an old name for a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Instructions to put a golden coin into circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: A threepenny bit was a pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to travel round and round something, which is to circulate around it.

clue.text: As Samson was when shorn of his locks?

definitions.text: As Samson was when shorn of his locks?

parts.words: As Samson was when shorn of his locks?
parts.note: Samson lost his strength when his hair was cut, so he was upset; read the word as 'dis-' (removed) plus 'tressed' (having tresses)

explanation.surface: A question about the biblical strongman's state after Delilah had his hair cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upset after losing his strength, Samson was also literally deprived of his tresses.

clue.text: Stable with one working horse

parts.note: a stall is a compartment in a stable
I is the Roman numeral for one
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A stable housing one horse that does a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse, so it is a type of horse.

clue.text: Class holds university debate

indicators.note: one word holds another when the second sits inside it

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A school class hosts a university debating event.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a 'form' is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting or medium for open discussion, so it stands for a debate.

clue.text: Lab equipment twice set back without objection on reflection

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the doubled piece goes around the other
the reversed piece is written down two times in a row
set back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a mirror image runs backwards, so the word for objection is reversed

parts.note: but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Lab gear that was put back twice without anyone objecting, after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; 'back' gives TES, doubled by 'twice', and 'on reflection' turns the objection round before it sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Test tubes are glass vessels used in laboratories, so they are lab equipment.

clue.text: Excluded lawyers' right to be in action

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
the Bar is the collective term for barristers

explanation.surface: Lawyers were shut out of their right to take legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the Bar' is the body of barristers, trial lawyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Debarred means barred or excluded from something.

clue.text: Afterwards? Dead right!

parts.note: the late someone is a dead person

explanation.surface: Someone checks the timing of a death and is told they are spot on.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, which is afterwards.

clue.text: One's belief in life and love accepted by boy and girl

indicators.note: the piece for love is taken in between the names of the boy and girl

parts.note: Phil is a boy's name
Sophy is a girl's name
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A person's creed about life and love, held by a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophy is a person's guiding outlook or principles on how to live.

clue.text: Designed shoe for dancers

indicators.note: something designed is shaped anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Footwear created for people who dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoofer is informal slang for a dancer, especially a professional tap or chorus dancer.

clue.text: No mouser, perhaps, but pretty big!

indicators.note: signals that the letters could be another arrangement, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A cat that is no good at catching mice may still be rather large.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means very large, a stronger synonym for big.

clue.text: They go round but don't join up

definitions.text: They go round but don't join up

parts.words: They go round but don't join up
parts.note: curves that keep circling without ever closing into a ring

explanation.surface: Things that keep circling without ever completing the loop.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirals wind round a centre, moving outward so the ends never meet as a circle's would.

clue.text: Confirm when definite

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
certain means definite

explanation.surface: Checking something is sure at the moment it becomes fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for sure, which is to confirm a fact.

clue.text: Leave one's pad, having to use the stairs?

definitions.text: Leave one's pad, having to use the stairs?

parts.words: Leave one's pad, having to use the stairs?
parts.note: a rocket leaves its launch pad; read the other way, a flat-dweller must walk down because the elevator is out of service

explanation.surface: Someone leaves their flat but must walk down because the elevator is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' is slang for a home and also a launch pad; in British English a lift is an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift-off is the moment a rocket leaves the launch pad, and a lift that is off forces you onto the stairs.

clue.text: Supply seafood without container

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the seafood goes around the container

parts.note: fish is food from the sea
an urn is a container

explanation.surface: Provide fish and chips with no takeaway box.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with something is to supply or provide it.

clue.text: Dash to get article into cheap production

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the rearranged letters
a production is something put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Rushing to put a piece into a low-budget staging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a verb of hurrying but is the noun for flair; 'production' reshuffles the letters into PACHE, and 'into' sets the article after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of flair or style matches panache, verve and flamboyance.

clue.text: Bill goes to North gate

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck up in public

explanation.surface: A man named Bill heads northwards to a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a back or side gate, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: Old-fashioned engine-driver set out before morning

indicators.note: letters that are out are not in their usual order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traditional train driver sets off before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam was the power that drove locomotives in the old days, so it is what drove the engine.

clue.text: Queen Elizabeth, right or wrong?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is Queen Elizabeth's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Asking whether Queen Elizabeth was correct or not.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, something wrong; the noun stands for 'a wrong'.

clue.text: Their depredations affect the stockholders

parts.note: 'stockholders' reads as shareholders but here means ranchers who own livestock, the victims of cattle thieves

explanation.surface: Raiders whose looting hurts investors in the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustlers steal cattle, so the owners of livestock are the ones who suffer.

clue.text: He acts as a substitute in practice

definitions.text: He acts as a substitute in practice

parts.words: He acts as a substitute in practice
parts.note: a doctor who stands in for another at a medical practice; 'in practice' seems to mean in reality

explanation.surface: Someone who in reality serves as a stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or clergyman temporarily covering for another in their practice.

clue.text: Press makes a German cross

explanation.surface: Pressure turns a German man angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Cross is a German military medal, so the metal gives the cross its name.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes is to iron them, and iron is what names the German military Iron Cross.

clue.text: Piggy is holding up another animal

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: porcine means pig-like

explanation.surface: A pig is propping up a different creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A porcupine is a spiny rodent, which is another animal besides the pig.

clue.text: I burn out in academic post

indicators.note: the word for burn is placed outside the I

parts.note: to char is to burn

explanation.surface: A lecturer declares they are burnt out in their university role.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a professorship, a senior academic position.

clue.text: Not far for cart to reverse

indicators.note: the word for cart is read backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads such as beer barrels

explanation.surface: A cart has only a short distance to back up.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is a short distance of three feet, so it suggests not far.

clue.text: Men on phone about an amazing spectacle

indicators.note: turned about, so these letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Men on the phone discuss an astonishing sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon is a remarkable or extraordinary thing, an amazing sight or event.
